output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss two hours ago in a 55-year-old is a potential central retinal artery occlusion or other vascular/retinal emergency requiring immediate emergency eye and stroke assessment.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that has not returned can be caused by a blocked retinal artery, which is treated like a stroke and is time-critical. Do not drive yourself; have someone take you or call 911, especially if you develop weakness, numbness, facial droop or trouble speaking.
differential: Retinal detachment or vitreous/retinal vascular event
